name: Figure
summary: Figure develops autonomous humanoid robots and the AI and manufacturing systems intended to deploy them at commercial scale.
overview: Figure is building general-purpose humanoid robots for industrial and commercial work.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Closed September 2025 at a $39B post-money valuation.

bull_case: A working humanoid platform could create a major new automation category across industrial and service labor.
bear_case: The business must turn impressive demonstrations into reliable, safe, and economic deployments at scale.
directory_notes: Helix AI platform and BotQ manufacturing.
Commercial deployment, reliability, and unit economics.

intelligence.description: Figure develops general-purpose humanoid robots, its Helix vision-language-action AI system, and BotQ manufacturing. The wager is that a single robotic form factor can learn enough tasks to earn a place in industrial and eventually consumer environments.
company: Founded in 2022, Figure is pursuing a humanoid robot that can operate in environments built for people. It combines mechanical hardware with Helix, an AI system intended to translate vision and language into robotic action.

The company is also building its own manufacturing capability through BotQ. The ambition is not a one-off research robot but a platform that can be produced in volume and taught new work through a common software and data stack.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Figure is one of the clearest private-market tests of whether embodied AI can become a commercial category. Its progress affects the outlook for automation suppliers, industrial software, sensor companies, semiconductors, and employers facing labor constraints.

changed.text: Raised $675M from a group that included major technology and industrial investors.
Introduced BotQ manufacturing plans and continued development of the Helix AI platform.
Closed more than $1B of committed Series C capital at a $39B post-money valuation.

takeaways: Figure is betting that humanoids can share a scalable AI and manufacturing platform across many tasks.
The Series C valuation embeds a large assumption about future deployment volume and economics.
Owning the robot, the AI stack, and manufacturing could create leverage if adoption happens.
Reliability, safety, service, and cost per useful hour are the questions that matter more than demonstrations.
